title: 2018 AMC 10B 16
statement:
Let \(a_1,\) \(a_2,\) \(\ldots,\) \(a_{2018}\) be a strictly increasing sequence of positive integers such that

\[a_1 + a_2 + \cdots + a_{2018} = 2018^{2018}.\]

What is the remainder when \(a_1^3 + a_2^3 + \cdots + a_{2018}^3\) is divided by \(6?\)

solutions.text: For any integer \(n,\) \(n^3 - n = (n-1)n(n+1)\) is a product of three consecutive integers, so it’s divisible by \(6.\) That means \(n^3 \equiv n \pmod 6.\) Summing, \(\sum a_i^3 \equiv \sum a_i\) \(= 2018^{2018} \pmod 6.\) Now \(2018 \equiv 2 \pmod 6,\) and powers of \(2\) mod \(6\) alternate \(2, 4, 2, 4, \ldots.\) The exponent \(2018\) is even, so \(2^{2018} \equiv 4 \pmod 6.\) The remainder is \(4.\) Therefore, the answer is E.
hints: \(n^3 \equiv n \pmod 6,\) because \(n^3 - n = (n-1)n(n+1)\) is a product of three consecutive integers
So the sum of cubes is congruent to \(2018^{2018} \pmod 6;\) reduce that modulo \(6\)
